claude.rationale: gap_45 = 1: a 49% fractional interest in the customer-facing asset (Greenway Properties) crossed the ownership boundary into the JV/subsidiary-REIT while the operating processes (property management, leasing, construction management) did NOT transfer — they remained with the Parkway subsidiary under services agreements, a documented product-vs-process mismatch at closing ("a fractional interest in the customer-facing asset crossed the boundary while the operating processes and the management organization that run them remained with the seller"). gap_mitigated = yes: the mismatch was contractually absorbed at closing via the property management, leasing and construction-management agreements and the Contribution/Direction Agreements bridging the shared substrate. gap_56 = 0: because the processes (T5) themselves did not transfer to the investors — both the operating processes and the management organization stayed together with the seller as general partner — there is no T5-without-T6 mismatch. T3 coded swap because a new legal vehicle (GWP JV LP / Subsidiary REIT) was formed to hold the asset. T2 T1 coded continue since Parkway retained 51% control and continued running day-to-day operations as general partner.

gemini.rationale: The slice explicitly states that a fractional 49% interest in the customer-facing asset (the Greenway Properties) crossed the ownership boundary to the investors (T4). However, the operating processes and management organization did not transfer; they remained with the seller, creating a structural gap between the asset and its operations (gap_45 = 1). Because both the processes and the people running them remained together with the seller, there is no mismatch between T5 and T6 (gap_56 = 0).

openai.rationale: A 49% interest in the customer-facing Greenway Properties crossed to the investors, while Parkway retained 51% control and the operating processes remained with Parkway, creating a product-versus-process structural gap at closing. That gap was contractually absorbed through property-management, leasing, construction-management, Contribution, and Direction Agreements [SRC: SEC accession 0001193125-17-130778, Form 8-K Items 1.01 and 2.01]. Because both the operating processes and the management organization running them remained with Parkway, no process-versus-organization gap is documented.
